summary: Describes the guidelines and process the IAB and the IESG use to select members of the IETF Administrative Oversight Committee, the body that oversees administrative support for the IETF. It is a Best Current Practice. It was replaced by RFC 8711.

plainLanguage.summary: Like the rules for picking the committee that looks after a club's money and paperwork. It says who chooses the members and how they go about it.

subtitle: How the IETF picks members of its administrative oversight committee.

tldr.problem: The IETF needs a transparent, fair process to select members of the IETF Administrative Oversight Committee, which oversees the administrative support organization.
tldr.mechanism: The IAB and IESG alternate in selecting one voting member each through a public call for nominations, review of candidates, and a formal selection process with a two-year term of office.
tldr.outcome: RFC 8711 later superseded this with a new administrative structure, but the process established clear procedures for committee selection.

today: RFC 4333 is a Best Current Practice that was obsoleted by RFC 8711, which established a new administrative structure for the IETF. The procedures in this RFC are no longer in use.

sections.title: The IAOC and Its Role
sections.content:
The IETF Administrative Oversight Committee (IAOC) is part of the IETF Administrative Support Activity (IASA), which provides the administrative structure to support the IETF standards process. The IAOC's core job is not to do administrative work directly, but to provide direction and oversight of the IETF Administrative Director and the IASA operations.

The IAOC has five main responsibilities: selecting and reviewing the IETF Administrative Director; reviewing administrative plans and contracts; monitoring whether the administrative functions meet community needs; reviewing budget proposals and financial reports; and ensuring the IASA operates transparently and publishes regular financial and operational reports to the community.
sections.plainLanguage: The IAOC is a small committee that watches over the people who handle the IETF's money and meetings. They make sure everything is done fairly and report back to everyone.

sections.title: Qualifications for IAOC Members
sections.content:
Candidates selected for the IAOC must understand the IETF and be familiar with administrative support needs. They must have knowledge of contracts and financial procedures, and understand the roles of both the IETF and the Internet Society in this activity.

Members are expected to fully participate in all committee meetings and activities, and be prepared to handle responsibilities such as setting administrative policies and overseeing administrative operations. Importantly, IAB-selected and IESG-selected members do not directly represent their parent bodies, but are accountable directly to the entire IETF community.
sections.plainLanguage: People on the committee need to know how the IETF works, understand money and contracts, and be able to go to meetings regularly. They work for the whole community, not just for the group that picks them.

sections.title: Nomination and Selection Process
sections.content:
The IAB and IESG alternate each year in making a public call for nominations on the ietf-announce mailing list. Self-nominations are allowed, and any IETF participant, including working group chairs and IAB or IESG members, are eligible. Candidates must provide their background and qualifications with their nomination.

The selecting body publishes the list of nominees before making a decision, allowing the community to submit relevant comments. The body then reviews the nominations and comments and makes its selection. To maintain integrity, IAB members who are nominated for an IAB-selected position recuse themselves from selection discussions, and the same applies for IESG members.
sections.plainLanguage: The IETF announces that they are looking for candidates and lets anyone apply, including themselves. The people voting on it hear from the community first, then pick someone.

sections.title: Term Length and Selection Schedule
sections.content:
Normally, a selected member serves a two-year term of office, seated at the first IETF meeting of every second year. The IAB and IESG alternate year by year in conducting selections. The selection process has two phases: 3 to 4 weeks for solicitation of nominations, followed by 3 to 4 weeks for review, deliberation, and selection. In November of each year, the selecting body announces the specific dates for that year's selection process.

If a member cannot complete their term, the selecting body may choose an interim replacement using an expedited process, or the next regularly scheduled selection can fill the vacancy instead.
sections.plainLanguage: Members serve for two years, and the IETF picks new ones every other year. The whole selection takes about two months: one month to ask for candidates, then one month to decide.
